data.description:
## Problem

Two operator-facing messages in `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py` still say that a re-clone makes the old environment's op-cert attestations unverifiable, with a `foreign_key` verdict at the claim and close gates:

- the `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` fsck line built by `divergence_report` ("Op-cert attestations signed by those identities cannot be verified here ... and must be re-earned");
- the mint warning built by `reidentification_warning` ("every op-cert attestation it signed is now unverifiable here (a `foreign_key` verdict at the claim/close gates) and must be re-earned").

Since commit `3bde5613718` (bug `c21f-6f29-5d2d-4a5a`, "Stop gating op-certs on signing environment") that is no longer true by default. `docs/concurrency.md` (the paragraph after the `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` description) says a re-clone no longer invalidates op-cert attestations, because an SSHSIG blob carries its public half (`envelope_key` trust basis). `src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json` says `foreign_key` now means no usable signer key, or that the opt-in `verify.require_environment` is set and the cert is from another environment.

So the code's messages contradict the docs and the verifier. An operator who reads them may re-run gates that do not need it.

## Approach

Reword both messages to the current policy. Attestations from the old identity still certify under the `envelope_key` basis. They become `foreign_key` only when `verify.require_environment` is set. Keep the carry-over remedy, since a re-clone still costs the audit trail and the ability to sign as the old identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Neither message claims that attestations become unverifiable by default; both name `verify.require_environment` as the condition for `foreign_key`.
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py` asserts the reworded text for both messages.
data.title: Re-clone messages claim attestations stop verifying
